title: session-fenced-rolling-cutover-with-telemetry-lock-and-rewind
author: Maya Chen
body: Motivation: production canary cutovers occasionally expose session-affinity regressions when a model swap drains existing sessions. This PR introduces a session-fenced rolling cutover executor that: 1) acquires a short-lived telemetry lock for a cohort during each step so metrics observed during a step cannot be overwritten by concurrent rollouts, 2) enforces session-fencing on swap so in-flight sessions are either pinned to the old model until completion or moved atomically to a warmed instance depending on policy, and 3) exposes a rewind handle for operator-driven fast revert (replayable snapshot of routing state). This reduces noisy telemetry and avoids mixing signals across overlapping rollouts. Changes included: - new orchestration executor (CutoverExecutor) that sequences cohort-level cutover with lock leases - session fencing mode (pin | migrate) with safe drain heuristics and KV-cache-aware handoff - telemetry lock on the metrics pipeline with lease and ownership tags - lightweight rewind journal that captures routing state + snapshot pointer for immediate revert - integration test harness for simulated multi-cohort traffic and smoke replay Checklist: - [x] CutoverExecutor implementation - [x] Session fence mechanics + migration path - [x] Telemetry lock integration and lease renewal - [x] Rewind journal and revert API - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Docs: rollout-runbook and operational playbook Notes: this is targeted at the hosted/dedicated control plane and is intentionally backwards-compatible by default; existing rollouts continue to use the previous executor unless customers opt-in via rollout.policy.cutover_strategy. Related linear: ENG-4321 (session fencing design), ENG-4380 (telemetry lock prototype). Rollout impact: opt-in only, no mandatory migration. See the runbook link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4321/session-fenced-cutover

review_comments: Evan Garcia: Nice separation of concerns. Two requests: (1) add invariants to CutoverExecutor docs about lease expiry behavior; (2) can we make the default pin timeout configurable per cohort?
Maya Chen (author): Responding: added invariants in doc comments and exposed cohort.timeout.pin in rollout policy. Updated tests to exercise shorter lease windows.
Priya Kapoor: Integration test looks comprehensive but I saw a flake when running the migration path under high concurrency. Please add a retry in the handoff path and a comment explaining tradeoffs.
Maya Chen (author): Added exponential backoff retry to handoff and extended test run to cover the flake. Also added a TODO to consider bounded retries in future work.
Liam O'Neil: Approving pending CI. Minor nit: prefer 30s default telemetry lock vs 60s. Not blocking.
release_notes: Introduces session-fenced rolling cutover executor (opt-in). Adds telemetry lock and rewind journal to allow safe cohort-level cutovers with operator-driven revert. Configuration: rollout.policy.cutover_strategy and rollout.policy.cohort.timeout.pin. See runbook for operational guidance.
files_excerpt: pkg/orchestrator/cutover_executor.go: CutoverExecutor sequences cohort steps, acquires telemetry lease, invokes sessionFence, then commit or rewind on failure.
pkg/orchestrator/session_fence.go: sessionFence handles 'pin' and 'migrate' modes; migrate warms target instance and atomically swaps session routing.
internal/telemetry/lock_manager.go: small lease-based lock with owner tags (rollout_id, cohort_id) and renewal loop. Uses metrics to tag timeseries with lock_owner.
docs/runbooks/rollout-session-fence.md: operational playbook describing how to run cutovers, interpret lock_owner metrics, and perform a rewind revert.
